### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary With `speculative-config {"method":"ngram"}` on a hybrid GDN/Mamba model, the XPU `gdn_attention` kernel asserts and the engine dies. The kernel requires a **uniform** speculative draft length across the batch; ngram produces a **ragged** one, because a partial n-gram match drafts fewer tokens than `num_speculative_tokens`. This is **not** the mixed prefill+decode batch case and **not** the empty-draft case. It reproduces with a single stream. ### Error ``` File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/_xpu_ops.py", line 171, in _gdn_attention_core_xpu_impl torch.ops._xpu_C.gdn_attention( RuntimeError: Expected spec_token == num_spec_decodes * (num_speculative_tokens + 1) to be true, but got false. ``` Reached via `qwen3_5.py:591 forward` → `qwen3_next.py:627 forward` → the AOT-compiled submodule → `_xpu_C.gdn_attention`. The engine does not recover: ``` EngineCore encountered a fatal error XPUWorker shutdown: cleaning up (rank=0, local_rank=0) vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError POST /v1/chat/completions -> 500 Application shutdown complete ``` ### Reproduction ```bash vllm serve /models/Qwen3.8-27B-GPTQ-Int4 \ --quantization gptq --dtype float16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --max-model-len 224000 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \ --max-num-seqs 1 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --speculative-config '{"method":"ngram","num_speculative_tokens":3,"prompt_lookup_min":3,"prompt_lookup_max":3}' ``` Then send ordinary generation requests over semi-repetitive text (code, config files, anything the drafter can partially match). The crash arrives within a few hundred generated tokens. **`--max-num-seqs 1` is deliberate.** The engine log at the moment of the crash shows `Running: 1 reqs`, so batching is not required to trigger it and limiting concurrency does not avoid it. ### Drafter state immediately before the crash ``` Mean acceptance length: 1.74 Accepted: 32 tokens · Drafted: 129 tokens Per-position acceptance rate: 0.395, 0.233, 0.116 Avg Draft acceptance rate: 24.8% ``` The falling per-position rate is the point: drafts routinely die part-way through, which is exactly the ragged-length condition. ### Why the input distribution matters (and how to get a false negative) We initially failed to reproduce this with a synthetic probe and briefly concluded the bug was gone. The probe used random-word prompts, which give the drafter either **no** match (drafts 0 → no speculative batch → harmless) or a **full** match (drafts exactly N → equality holds). Only a **partial** match produces a draft of length 1 or 2, which is what breaks the equality. So a reproduction attempt needs content the drafter can *partially* match. Random tokens will pass and prove nothing. ### Why this is distinct from the existing issues - **#53077** (merged 2026-08-20) resets `num_spec_decodes` when *every* scheduled draft count is zero. Our build contains it and still asserts — this is the ragged case inside a *non-empty* schedule, not the all-zero case. - **#38196** / **#36917** / **#36918** are mixed decode + spec_decode *batch* problems. This reproduces at `Running: 1 reqs`. - **#53051** is a prefill misdispatched into the spec-decode cudagraph, a different mechanism with a different symptom (silent bad output, not an assert). - **#53928** is the `causal_conv1d` mixed prefill+decode error, fixed in vllm-xpu-kernels 0.1.14.1 — this build has that fix. ### Notes - `prompt_lookup_min == prompt_lookup_max` does **not** avoid it. Those bound the match length searched, not the drafter's ability to emit a shorter draft (or none) when no match of that length exists. - `suffix` should fail identically, being variable-length by the same nature. - MTP is unaffected, since it always drafts exactly `num_speculative_tokens`. - Consequence on XPU: **MTP is the only usable speculation method for this model family**, and MTP is the one that interacts badly with prefix caching (see #50897 / #52244 / #53479). ### Suggested direction Either pad ragged speculative batches to a uniform draft length before the kernel call, or relax the kernel's equality to accept a per-request draft-length vector. The all-zero case already has precedent in #53077; this is the same class of problem one step further along. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
